primitives.name: Role-Based Workload Distribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: For instance, a rusher will never be called upon to drop-kick a goal, nor will a half be forced to snap-back the ball.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_i': 'Role identifier for player i (dimensionless)', 'W_i': 'Workload assigned to player i (work units)', 'T_i': 'Time allocated to role R_i (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are assigned roles with fixed functional responsibilities; workload is distributed to prevent cross-role exhaustion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When W_i exceeds capacity T_i, resulting in reduced performance or injury risk.

layer2.mapping: Each player's role corresponds to a kernel function in GSE's state transition matrix, where workload distribution mirrors conditional probability distributions in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Performance metrics such as sprint speed, error rate, and substitution frequency.

primitives.name: Individual Role Exhaustion Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: There still remains the possibility of giving any one of these men so much work of his own special kind to perform as will exhaust him, and thus make it impracticable to call upon him when he is most needed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_i': 'Exhaustion level of player i (normalized unit)', 'C_i': 'Capacity of player i for role R_i (work units)', 'A_i': 'Actual workload applied to player i (work units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Exhaustion occurs when A_i > C_i, leading to diminished utility in critical moments.
primitives.breakdown_regime: E_i approaches 1.0, indicating near-complete depletion of role-specific capability.

layer2.mapping: Exhaustion threshold becomes a derived kernel in GSI's predictive model, influencing agent behavior via dynamic fatigue scoring.
layer2.telemetry: Heart rate variability, sprint frequency, and time-to-substitution data.

primitives.name: Strategic Single-Player Overreliance
primitives.verbatim_quote: Year after year has the "one man" game been attempted, and year after year it has brought to grief the team attempting it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'Single-player reliance strategy (binary)', 'F(S)': 'Failure probability of S (dimensionless)', 'M': 'Team performance metric (normalized)'}
primitives.assumptions: Overreliance on one player leads to systemic failure due to lack of redundancy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As S → 1, F(S) → 1, causing M to degrade significantly.

layer2.mapping: The 'one man' strategy maps to a high-variance, low-entropy policy in GSE’s decision tree, where failure is deterministic under repeated application.
layer2.telemetry: Team win-loss ratio, substitution timing, and variance in key performance indicators.

The foundational principle of role specialization in football is mathematically modeled as a constrained optimization problem, where each player's workload W_i is bounded by their role-specific capacity C_i. This ensures that no single player is overburdened beyond their functional limits, thereby maintaining team resilience. The system exhibits a dual structure: one where regularity is enforced through role segregation (e.g., rushers do not drop-kick), and another where failure modes arise from overreliance on singular individuals. The latter is a known instability in systems with low entropy and high variance—akin to a non-redundant control loop. In GSI, this manifests as a probabilistic model of player fatigue and substitution likelihood. In GSE, it translates into a state-space transition graph where each node represents a player's role state, and transitions are governed by workload thresholds. The failure mode of overreliance is captured by a binary variable S, where S=1 implies a single-player strategy, and F(S) approaches unity as S increases, indicating increasing risk of catastrophic failure.
